title: BODY LOCK PILLAR REINF BRACE SUPPORT & LOCATING PIN BRACKET
summary: Steel lock pillar (B-pillar) area of the body: the lock pillar brace support [1] (the cross brace behind the seats) and the folding top support [2] are spot-welded to the lock pillar reinforcement. On convertibles (19467) a nut [4] in a welded retainer [3] is added, and a locating pin bracket [7] is screwed with screws [6] (60-75 lb-in) into a tapping plate [5] on the lock pillar; the bracket is left loose until after body drop. View B gives the drilling for the tapping plate holes.

fastening.qty: 10 places (A1); 5 places 1.75 pitch (A2) + 5 places 1.00 pitch (A3) each side
fastening.note: Spot welds. A1 is at the inboard end of the brace (shown near the car centerline, .25 from CL); A2/A3 run down the lock pillar.
Spot welds; folding top support [2] on the inboard face of the lock pillar reinforcement.
Spot welds. Retainer [3] holds nut [4] on the lock pillar (convertible).
Nut [4] is caged by retainer [3] near the top of the lock pillar (19467).
View A (19467): screws [6] go through the side of bracket [7] and the lock pillar wall into tapping plate [5] behind it. Leave [7] loose until after body drop.
View A: rivet [8] at the top hole of the lock pillar wall, apparently retaining tapping plate [5] (hole alignment lines only).
